segs.utf8: Hey, it's Mark.

Now, I don't usually do a lot of 
programming related content on this channel,

despite the fact that programming is of course 
An essential part of any game maker's toolkit.

But that's just because I am far 
from an expert on this subject.
I mean, the code bases for my two video games,

Mind Over Magnet and Word Play, 
are basically held together
with sticks and the glue.

But there is one aspect of Word Play's 
programming that I'm actually really

proud of, and that's the way I 
implemented the game's modifiers.
So - for context.

Word Play is a vocabulary roguelike 
where you spell words to score points.

And then you can unlock perks that let 
you bend the rules and score even bigger.
These perks come in three flavours.
Gifts typically add more letters to your bag.
Upgrades let you change and improve your tiles.

And modifiers are the passive perks that 
give big benefits under the right conditions.

Like... this one that multiplies your score 
by 1.5 if the first letter is a vowel.

So they're basically the relics from Slay 
the Spire or the Jokers from Balatro.

Now when I first started making the game I had 
no idea how I would implement these modifiers.
There wasn't an obvious and easy way to do it.

But, ultimately, I came up with a 
system that I'm really happy with.

One that fits the requirements for the system, 
can be easily scaled to fit all 120 modifiers

in the game, and makes it effortless to 
test, change, and debug the lot of them.

So I'm hoping this might prove interesting 
or helpful or inspirational to, let's say,
a beginner or intermediate level programmer.

to see what it takes to implement 
a somewhat complex system into

a real life video game that's 
currently available on Steam.
If that sounds good, then let's jump in.

A quick note that I'll be talking 
about it in the context of making
the game in Unity, because that's what I used.

But the basic idea should apply 
to pretty much any engine.

So the modifiers in Word Play touch 
so many aspects of the game, with modifiers

that fiddle with refreshes and bonus rounds and 
special tiles and the basic rules of spelling.
And I'll come to that - but for now,

let's make things simple by looking at the 
ones that impact the way your word is scored.
Like - that modifier I showed earlier:

"If the first letter is a Vowel, 
multiply the Final Score by 1.5".
How would we implement that?
Well, first I'll write some code to tally up the

word's initial score by adding up the 
points on all of the submitted tiles.
